findings.reason: §4's done-when items 1, 2, 3 and 6 (zellij survives viewer loss, runtime dir + cross-session messaging, step reaps a detached child, `uv run --no-sync` through the launcher) become verification of an existing shipped module rather than construction, which changes the plan's scope, its dependencies and its effort estimate.
findings.text: §4 proposes building "a launcher" that runs zellij inside the allocation's batch step, creates a private node-local runtime directory on `/tmp` and points `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` at it, and starts each session as an own-step; that is exactly `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:1` (its module docstring and its `session`/`spawn`/`reload`/`stop` FIFO), driven by the sbatch batch script at `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:127`–`:153` — and §4's own audit line ("the launcher that runs zellij inside the batch step is not built") is stale against the shipped code.

findings.reason: the plan must name which allocation owner it extends (fleet_node's `sbatch` submission, or a change of placement's scheduler away from `salloc --no-shell`), because the re-hold path it names structurally cannot satisfy §4's requirement and the author would otherwise discover this at first implementation.
findings.text: the plan's §4 requires that "the re-hold path that `the-fleet-shares-one-allocation` uses must create the batch script that starts the zellij server", but that path is `placement.ensure_reservation` (`reckon/crew/placement.py:583`) which submits `salloc` with `RESERVATION_NO_SHELL_OPTION` (`reckon/crew/placement.py:52`–`:54`) — an allocation with no batch step, hence nowhere to start a zellij server at all; the mechanism that already submits an allocation whose batch step runs the supervisor is `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py` (`generate_hold_script` at `:127`, `submit` at `:167`), and `placement._adopt_live_fleet_allocation` (`reckon/crew/placement.py:488`) already reaches across to it.

findings.reason: the plan should extend the cgroup-resolution owner (`host.host_facts` / `summary._user_slice_dir`) to expose the throttled counters, so that "which cgroup" is decided once and both sides of the report read the counter file through the same owner; a parallel reader duplicates the resolution and the two can disagree about which cgroup was sampled.
findings.text: §1 and §5 measure the throttled fraction "read from whichever cgroup is running them at the time, naming the counter file it read on each side", but the decision of *which cgroup* a process runs in is already owned by `reckon/host.py` (`_own_cgroup_components` `:105`, `_cgroup_names_job` `:105`, `_inside_the_job`) and `reckon/crew/summary.py` (`LOGIN_CGROUP_ROOT` `:82`, `SELF_CGROUP_PATH` `:87`, `_user_slice_dir` `:191`); no `cpu.stat`/`nr_throttled`/`throttled_usec` reader exists anywhere in reckon (grep of `reckon/` returns only an unrelated comment), so the plan adds a reader rather than extending the owner.

findings.reason: the proof is only valid against the composer that actually placed the worker; naming one owner removes the ambiguity, or everything else the plan re-wraps over this twice-implemented invocation without saying why neither existing composer can be extended.
findings.text: placement into the shared allocation already has two composers of the same `srun --overlap --jobid=<id>` step invocation: `placement.step_prefix`/`reservation_step_argv` (`reckon/crew/placement.py:231`, `:840`, used by dispatch) and `fleet_node.placement_argv` (`reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:326`, used by `reckon fleet-node place` at `reckon/cli.py:633`); §3/§5's proof ("a live worker's job id is the job id of the published reservation") has to read the same owner that placed the worker, and the plan names neither.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes no new module; its launcher maps onto the existing deep module `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`, whose FIFO interface (`session`/`spawn`/`reload`/`stop`) hides the batch step, zellij servers and runtime directory behind four verbs.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 requires the re-hold path to create a batch script that starts the zellij server, but the path it names submits `salloc --no-shell` (no batch step), while the batch-step owner `reckon/crew/fleet_node.py` already exists and is not cited.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §5 is operational (place the fleet, measure, prove) and no section names a new public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family it adds.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes a "launcher" (§4) and a throttled-fraction cgroup reader (§1) without citing the mechanisms that already implement them, `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py` and `reckon/host.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan's placement/measurement proof leans on machinery that already has two composers of the same `srun --overlap --jobid=` invocation (`placement.step_prefix` and `fleet_node.placement_argv`) without naming which one owns the step it proves.
